relationship: Partially independent. The Zurich lemmatisation is a modern analysis; the padapatha is the ancient Sakalya word-analysis. They agree on segmentation but the padapatha is unaccented at the ambiguous points and cannot disambiguate pur- from puras / pura.
effect_on_status: Supports PUR-010 as a genuine recall check. Does not make PUR-003 double-sourced, because the padapatha cannot confirm the 48 ambiguous cases.
notes: See PUR-009 and PUR-010.

relationship: Arnold's Popular stratum and the book-order instrument are not independent measures of lateness: 61.3% of Popular-stratum tokens sit in book 10, and book 10 is 46.7% Popular.
effect_on_status: A claim resting on agreement between the two instruments is single-sourced at the late end.
notes: Recorded as PUR-021. This is the specific trap that produced correction C-05 in 01-INHERITED.

relationship: The retroflexion classification in DME-003 to DME-007 depends on the Zurich lemma citation form, which is a modern normalisation. Word-initial position, in particular, is a property of the citation form and not directly of any attested text token.
effect_on_status: DME-007 stays VERIFIED as a statement about the lemma inventory. It would need re-checking against surface forms before being restated as a claim about the recited text.
notes: Sandhi produces surface retroflexes at word boundaries that the lemma layer normalises away. The claim is scoped to lemmas for that reason, and says so.

relationship: Both trace to Krishnamurti 2003. Glottolog's North Dravidian node cites Krishnamurti 2003 and no other work (nort2698/md.ini, subrefs), and so do its Central and South Dravidian nodes; DravLex's cognate coding lists Krishnamurti 2003 among its five underlying sources (cldf/sources.bib). Krishnamurti 2003 has never been read in this project: it stands at 'Named, not read' (IH-237, 01-INHERITED/claude-project-handoff.md L451).
effect_on_status: Glottolog is NOT independent confirmation of the North Dravidian subgroup; it is a re-encoding of one book. Any claim that 'the standard classification and the comparative dataset agree' is single-sourced and capped at PROVISIONAL. It also means the cognate dataset is not independent of the hypothesis it is used to test here, which is why DMB-020 is reported as a bound and not as a test.
notes: The one place the dependency does NOT hold: the Kurux-Malto node below North Dravidian cites Kobayashi and Tirkey 2017 at pages 11-14, a different author and a different work. The lower node therefore has a second source; the top node, the one that attaches Brahui, does not.

relationship: DravLex's cognate judgements list Burrow and Emeneau 1961, the first edition of the Dravidian Etymological Dictionary, among their sources. SRC-037 is DEDR, the 1984 second edition, which is unreachable (HOLD-002).
effect_on_status: DravLex gives partial and indirect access to the DED cognate judgements for 100 concepts across 20 varieties. It does NOT lift HOLD-002: it carries no entry numbers, no etymologies, no Old Indo-Aryan comparanda and no reconstruction, which are the things HOLD-002 needs. Claims requiring a DEDR entry number stay HELD.
notes: Recorded so that a later reader does not treat SRC-049 as having closed HOLD-002. It narrows the hold's scope for one specific question - relative cognate sharing among attested varieties - and for nothing else.

relationship: The retrieved DEDR table is a re-parse of the DSAL digitization of Burrow and Emeneau 1984. DSAL is EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the intermediate stage cannot be inspected.

relationship: DEDR and CDIAL are not independent. Turner cites DED throughout, and Burrow and Emeneau's Dravidian Borrowings from Indo-Aryan is built against Indo-Aryan; several CDIAL Dravidian attributions are credited to Burrow's own papers (BSOAS 12, TPS 1945, TPS 1946).
effect_on_status: A word attributed to Dravidian by Turner and found in DEDR is ONE source, not two. No confirmation may be claimed from their agreement.
notes: Visible in the brackets counted for DE-M-002, e.g. CDIAL 16 and 50, both 'Burrow, BSOAS 12, 365'.

relationship: Grassmann 1876-7 translation and Grassmann Woerterbuch zum Rig-Veda are the same author, working the same decade on the same text. The dictionary glosses fixed the pur- family boundary (PUR-006, 04-AUDITS/rigveda-pur-family-method.md section 3); the translation renders the same word in running text.
effect_on_status: Caps any claim resting on both at the standing of one source. A translation agreeing with the dictionary that licensed the lemma selection is not corroboration; it is one judgement expressed twice.
notes: Load-bearing for the constitution section 7 translation standard on pur-. When counting how many translators render pur- as fort/Burg/castle, Grassmann must not be counted as an independent vote alongside the Grassmann gloss that defined the family.

relationship: stanza_properties.json carries Arnold, Sketch of the Historical Grammar of the Rig and Atharva Vedas, 1897 (JAOS 18:203-353). strata.json carries Arnold, Vedic Metre in its Historical Development, 1905. Same author, eight years apart, on the same chronological question from two evidence classes (grammar, metre).
effect_on_status: The arnold column of stanza_properties is NOT an independent check on the register stratum column. Agreement between them is one scholar being consistent with himself.
notes: Recorded before the columns are used, because DEP-004 and correction C-05 record this trap already having been sprung once. The columns of stanza_properties independent of Arnold are grassmann, oldenberg, wuest and witzel.

relationship: Elizarenkova 1989-1999 was made with Geldner 1951 in view and cites it throughout; the VedaWeb bundle asserts independent-witness status for neither.
effect_on_status: Agreement between Geldner and Elizarenkova on a rendering is weaker evidence than two independent translations agreeing. Not zero - Elizarenkova departs from Geldner in places, and a DISAGREEMENT between them is informative.
notes: Directionally asymmetric: their disagreement counts for more than their agreement. Recorded so a tally of translators is not read as a tally of evidence.

relationship: Same repository at the same commit d3eb8af, fetched a third time. SRC-085 re-verifies the strata.json checksum and reproduces the 164,758-token extraction; it retrieves no new material.

notes: Recorded so the varna census (03-REGISTERS/rigveda-varna.csv) cannot later be read as corroborated by three retrievals. What SRC-085 establishes is reproducibility of the extraction, which is a property of the method, not independent support for the corpus.

JAMBU's README states it: dedr.csv from a 2013 SQL database scraped from the online version and now deprecated; dedr_new.csv from parse.py scraping burrow_query.py over 514 pages. effect_on_status: They count as ONE source. Their agreement - both give 82% of Brahui roots with a Tamil cognate - is NOT independent confirmation and may not be used to weigh against the site's 73%. What their agreement measures is that the DSAL web pages did not change much between 2013 and 2026.

The two-way framing 'two digitizations disagree' treats the DSAL lineage as one voice, which is right; this row records WHY it is one voice, so that a later reader meeting three tables does not count three votes. relationship: One author, two works: Arnold 1897 'Sketch' and Arnold 1905 'Vedic Metre'. The 1897 late-addition marks and the 1905 metrical strata are separate publications eight years apart, not separate instruments.
effect_on_status: The Arnold 1897 column must never be counted as corroboration of the Arnold 1905 strata. Its Popular enrichment of 6.75x (RCI-006) is the highest of the five and is reported as the same-author ceiling against which the other four are read, not as evidence.
notes: SRC-095, the DCS transcription of Arnold 1905's lexical word lists, is a third piece of the same body and is likewise not independent of SRC-023. Duplicate of DEP-022, which main logged for the same reason on the same day from a different branch. Two sessions set the same trap for themselves and both caught it. Kept as a separate row because it records what the duplication costs a different set of claims - RCI-006 and RCI-008, where the Arnold 1897 enrichment of 6.75x is the same-author ceiling the other four instruments are read against - and because rows are not removed from this file. Cite DEP-022 as the first record.
